extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners working on text summarization, evaluation, and large language models (especially news summarization)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating concise, factual news summaries that cover fine-grained news elements (following the Lasswell Communication Model) and that can be produced or assessed using large language models and chain-of-thought methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and key-idea coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic summarization generates concise summaries that contain key ideas of source documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries should be brief while including the essential ideas from the source; this is the basic goal motivating benchmark and method design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factuality (avoidance of hallucination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference summaries of common datasets are noisy mainly in terms of factual hallucination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation and dataset construction should emphasize factual correctness — summaries must not introduce unsupported facts or distort source information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of information redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference summaries suffer from information redundancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good summaries should avoid repeating the same information and should present each element once succinctly; datasets and metrics should penalize redundant content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element-aware coverage (Lasswell Communication Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference summaries should focus on more fine-grained news elements objectively and comprehensively, following the 'Lasswell Communication Model' proposed by Lasswell (1948).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate summaries on their inclusion and treatment of discrete news elements (e.g., actor, action, channel/audience/effect as per Lasswell); datasets annotated by experts should capture these element-level requirements to allow finer-grained assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with human preference / human writing mindset
rubrics_metrics.description: There were inconsistent results between human preference and automatic evaluation metrics for LLMs' zero-shot summaries in prior work; the study aims to align evaluation with expert human writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation protocols and reference summaries should be constructed so that metrics correlate with human judgments and the human approach to writing summaries; human-aligned test sets are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-shot LLM summarization capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation of the surprising zero-shot summary ability of LLMs when evaluated on the new element-aware test sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether LLMs can produce high-quality summaries without task-specific fine-tuning; benchmarking should distinguish zero-shot performance and consider dataset suitability for revealing true capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of chain-of-thought (SumCoT) to elicit stepwise summarization
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary Chain-of-Thought (SumCoT) is proposed to elicit LLMs to generate summaries step by step, helping them integrate more fine-grained details of source documents into final summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage multi-step generation processes (e.g., planning or element-by-element extraction) to improve coverage of fine-grained elements and better mirror human writing processes; evaluate whether stepwise methods increase alignment with human judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic metric: ROUGE-L improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental results report improvements in ROUGE-L (e.g., +4.33/+4.77 on two datasets) as a numeric evaluation signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ROUGE-L as one automatic metric for lexical/overlap quality, but interpret improvements in conjunction with element-aware, human-aligned evaluations due to possible metric-human discrepancies.
